chapter: Photographs: Eddie Miller, Shields and Willow band
title: 1931 newspaper photo: Harry Shields, Lester Nelson, Bobby Willow's band
summary: Sal and the interviewer identify the players in a 1931 photo, including Shields, Nelson, Willie Guitart, Johnny Cottrell, and Sal's big bass drum.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Buzzy Willow's in the orchestra, well I'm going to tell you. It says, this is from the Times picking in October the 26th, it looks like. Oh, yeah. 1931.
Yeah. And it's, can't see it when he paid, you know. Let's see, I can't recognize anybody in there, my eyes are not that good.
Well, you know a couple of them. Yeah. Well, here's Harry Shields. On the right. Playing out of time. Oh.

Tenor. Tenor. Looks like he's got a clarinet too, huh? Right. Mr. Pettit, to get a megaphone, cut the hose out and put on a megaphone, you know, clarinet together. It's the higher shield, Lester Nelson, me, with the spanzer. That's a big bass drum, 28 inches.
You say you had a 30 inch at one time, with a track though. That's right. But you weren't as good as Willie Guitart. No, I didn't steal the thing.

I was talking about it. Willie Guitart live on Music Street and played bass. And this was the leader, Bobby Williams, Bobby Willow. He played the banjo. You know the stuff? You know the music? I've heard of him, but I've never met him.
This is Johnny Cottrell. Oh yeah, I know Johnny Cottrell. I see him once every few years. And the tuba player, Truth Upon.
Oh, Willie? Willie Brown. Yeah. And Lester Nelson, you say played clarinet and alto both? Right.
And tenor. I never heard much about his tenor playing. I know he's supposed to be very good. That's fine.
